hypotheses.reasoning: audit-consumer (v3.23.3) hits an unhandled RangeError (Maximum call stack size exceeded) in expandReferences while processing msg-982640 at offset 620792. The process exits with code 1 and restarts, but on every restart it resumes at the same committed offset 620792 and fails on the same message again, so the consumer is stuck in a CrashLoop and audit.events lag grows. Three crash/restart cycles are visible (#214, #220, #226), and the restart at #237/#238 still resumes at offset 620792. Upstream services (account-svc, auth-svc, edge-proxy, session-cache, accounts-db) show no errors, and accounts-db vacuum and checkpoint lines look routine, so the fault is isolated to this one message. No deploy lines were found, so a release was not the trigger. The message content (likely a deeply nested or self-referencing reference structure) is the probable trigger for the recursion.

v3.23.3 is the version running at the crash. A release with unbounded recursion in expandReferences would also produce a stack overflow, but no deploy event appears in the logs, and the failure is tied to one specific message offset rather than to all traffic, so this is less likely than a poison message.

verdict.recommendedAction: Skip or quarantine msg-982640 (offset 620792) on audit.events, for example by moving it to a dead-letter topic or advancing the consumer group offset past 620792, so audit-consumer can drain the backlog. Then inspect that message's payload for the recursive reference structure, and make expandReferences depth-safe or reject such messages with a handled error instead of crashing. Add a handler that dead-letters messages that throw so one bad record cannot restart the consumer in a loop.
